events.title: Lot welcomes the two angels in Sodom
events.narrative_summary: The two angels reach Sodom at evening, where Lot sits in the gate. He bows to them and urges them to lodge in his house; they first refuse, then come in and eat the feast and unleavened bread he prepares.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'At even' (19:1) read as the same day as the visit to Abraham, which began at noon (18:1); Rashi says the angels waited for Abraham's plea (Sforno: they entered only once his pleading had ended). Anchored on the end of Gen 18:33 at EREV (18:00). Three hours for the greeting, persuasion and meal; margin 1 hour.

events.title: The men of Sodom surround Lot's house
events.narrative_summary: Before bedtime, every man of Sodom, young and old, surrounds the house and demands that Lot bring out his guests. Lot goes out, offers his two daughters instead, and is pressed against the door.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Before they lay down' (19:4): right after the meal, the same night; anchored on the meal's END with no delay. The confrontation takes about half an hour; margin an hour.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: Before they lay down; this night

events.title: The angels pull Lot in and strike the crowd blind
events.narrative_summary: The men inside pull Lot back into the house and shut the door, and strike the men at the door with blindness, so that they weary themselves looking for the entrance.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediate response to the pressing at the door (19:9); starts the moment the previous scene ends. The weariness of the blind men could last longer, but the event itself is marked as ten minutes.

events.title: The angels tell Lot to bring out his family
events.narrative_summary: The men ask Lot whom he has in the city and tell him to bring them out, since they are about to destroy the place, sent by the LORD because the outcry has grown great.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Spoken once the crowd is blind, still in the night; 'and the men said' (19:12) follows without a gap. Ten minutes; margin 30 minutes.

events.title: Lot warns his sons-in-law, who think he is joking
events.narrative_summary: Lot goes out and tells the men who are to marry his daughters to leave because the LORD is about to destroy the city, but they take him for a jester.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: It happens in the night before dawn (19:15 'when the dawn rose' follows). One hour for the errand; margin 2 hours because the text does not say how long it took.

events.title: At dawn the angels seize Lot's hand and lead the family out
events.narrative_summary: As dawn rises the angels press Lot to take his wife and two daughters. When he lingers they take hold of the four by the hand, out of the LORD's mercy, set them outside the city, and tell them to flee to the hills without looking back.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'When the dawn rose' (19:15): SHACHAR, 05:30, after the night events. Radak: at the time the dawn rose. An hour for the lingering and leading out; margin 30 minutes. Verse 19:17 is the same scene, outside the city.

events.title: Lot begs to flee to little Zoar and is granted it
events.narrative_summary: Lot objects that he cannot reach the hills and asks to flee to a small nearby city. The angel grants it, says he cannot act until Lot arrives, and the city is named Zoar.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: A dialogue directly after being led out (19:17), still around first light. Twenty minutes; margin 30 minutes.

events.title: Lot enters Zoar as the sun rises over the land
events.narrative_summary: The sun has come out over the earth when Lot enters Zoar.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'The sun was risen upon the earth when Lot entered Zoar' (19:23): the text's time word fixes the arrival at about sunrise, not at the end of a long march. Lot himself calls Zoar 'near to flee unto' (19:20), so the flight is short: about half an hour after the plea ends (about 06:50), arriving about 07:20. Margin 90 minutes keeps the latest arrival at about 08:50, within the third hour (09:00) of Targum Pseudo-Jonathan, which has the sun come out 'at the end of three hours'. The straight-line 19 km (about 24 km by road, about 5 hours at 'hurry') depends on a site for Zoar of confidence 0.35, so the text wins over that figure.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: The sun was risen on the earth

events.title: The LORD rains sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah
events.narrative_summary: The LORD rains sulfur and fire from heaven on Sodom and Gomorrah and overthrows the cities, the whole plain, their inhabitants and the growth of the ground.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The angel said he could do nothing until Lot arrived (19:22), so the destruction starts the moment the entry into Zoar ends. Three hours, a rough estimate with a margin of an hour. Tier DAY_SEQUENCE: the text names no hour.

events.title: Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt
events.narrative_summary: Lot's wife looks back from behind him and becomes a pillar of salt.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Anchored on the start of the destruction, since the text offers no other hour. She was behind Lot (Ramban), so she cannot have been far in distance from Zoar. Margin one hour.

events.title: Abraham sees the smoke of the plain rise like a furnace
events.narrative_summary: Abraham rises early and goes to the place where he stood before the LORD. He looks down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and sees smoke rising like a furnace. The narrator adds that God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out of the overthrow.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Rose early in the morning' (19:27): BOKER, 06:00, the first morning after the destruction (which begins around noon, so the same morning is impossible). The smoke can still be rising a day later. Verse 19:29 is the narrator's summary of the whole event.

events.title: Lot goes up from Zoar and lives in a cave with his daughters
events.narrative_summary: Lot, afraid to live in Zoar, goes up and settles in the hill country, in a cave with his two daughters.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No delay is stated. I guessed two months after the destruction with margin two months; the event is the move itself (one day), not the whole stay. The tier REGNAL_YEAR reflects only that the whole chapter falls in Abraham's year 99-100.

events.title: Lot's daughters make him drunk and the elder lies with him
events.narrative_summary: The elder daughter tells the younger that no man is left to give them children, proposes to make their father drink wine and lie with him. That night they make him drink, and the elder lies with him; he does not know.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time is given beyond 'that night'. Guessed one month after the move to the cave ends (margin one month); starts at EREV and lasts ten hours of the night.

events.title: The next night the younger daughter lies with Lot
events.narrative_summary: On the morrow the elder tells the younger to do the same the next night. They make their father drink again and the younger lies with him; both daughters conceive.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'On the morrow' (19:34): counted from the end of the first night (about 04:00); the next EREV, 18:00 the same calendar day, begins the second night. Ten hours; margin two hours.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: On the morrow; that night also

events.title: The daughters bear Moab and Ben-ammi
events.narrative_summary: The elder bears a son and names him Moab, father of the Moabites; the younger bears Ben-ammi, father of the Ammonites.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Nine months after the conceptions, estimated; margin one month. Both births are treated as one event since the text does not separate them; the elder is listed first.

causal_edges.causal_explanation: God sends Lot out because he remembered Abraham (19:29), the one who had pleaded for the city.
The men who turn toward Sodom (18:22) are the two angels who arrive there at evening (19:1).
With the crowd disabled, the angels have time to tell Lot to bring out his family (19:12).
Once outside and told to flee to the hills, Lot objects and asks for Zoar instead (19:17-20).
The angels declare 'we are about to destroy this place' (19:13), and the LORD rains fire on the cities (19:24).
Lot passes on the angels' warning to his sons-in-law (19:14).
Once the strangers lodge with Lot, the men of Sodom hear of them and surround the house (19:4).
Both daughters conceive by their father (19:36) and bear Moab and Ben-ammi (19:37-38).
The smoke Abraham sees rising like a furnace is the result of the overthrow (19:28).
Lot fears to dwell in Zoar (19:30), implied to be in the wake of the destruction nearby.
The angel says nothing can be done until Lot arrives in Zoar (19:22), and the destruction follows (19:24).
The request is granted, and Lot enters Zoar (19:21-23).
Isolated in the cave, the daughters see no man left to give them children (19:31).
The crowd presses to break the door, so the guests pull Lot in and strike the men at the door with blindness (19:9-11).

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Children of Ammon', the people descended from Ben-ammi.
entities.summary_bio: The nation east of the Jordan, traced here to Ben-ammi, son of Lot and his younger daughter.
The nation east of the Dead Sea, traced here to Moab, son of Lot and his elder daughter.

entities.etymology_meaning: A descriptive group, named for their relation to Lot.
entities.summary_bio: The men engaged or married to Lot's daughters in Sodom. When Lot warns them to leave, they take him for a jester and stay behind.

entities.canonical_name: The cave in the hills above Zoar
entities.etymology_meaning: A descriptive name; the text says only 'a cave' in 'the mountain' (hehar).
entities.summary_bio: The cave in the hill country where Lot and his daughters live after leaving Zoar, out of fear, and where the events of 19:31–38 take place.

entities.etymology_meaning: The city gate, the place of public business and judgment in an ancient town.
entities.summary_bio: The gate of Sodom, where Lot is sitting when the two angels arrive at evening.
Lot's house in Sodom, where he hosts the two angels and which the men of the city surround that night.

entities.etymology_meaning: 'Son of my people' (or 'of my kinsman'); the name signals his kinship with Lot's family.
entities.summary_bio: Son of Lot's younger daughter by her own father. The text calls him the father of the Ammonites 'to this day'.

entities.etymology_meaning: Unnamed; the text calls her 'the firstborn' (habbekhirah).
entities.summary_bio: The elder of Lot's two unmarried daughters, offered by Lot to the mob of Sodom and rescued with him. In the cave she proposes the plan to preserve her father's line, lies with him first, and bears Moab.

entities.etymology_meaning: Unnamed in the text; she is identified only by her husband.
entities.summary_bio: Lot's wife, brought out of Sodom with her husband and two daughters at the angels' urging. Warned not to look back, she looks back from behind Lot and becomes a pillar of salt.

entities.etymology_meaning: Unnamed; the text calls her 'the younger' (hatstsa'irah).
entities.summary_bio: The younger of Lot's two unmarried daughters, offered to the mob of Sodom and rescued with Lot. She joins her sister's plan, lies with her father on the second night, and bears Ben-ammi.

entities.etymology_meaning: Popularly read as 'from the father' (me-av), a folk etymology matching the story; the origin of the name is otherwise uncertain.
entities.summary_bio: Son of Lot's elder daughter by her own father. The text calls him the father of the Moabites 'to this day'.

entities.etymology_meaning: Gofrit, 'sulfur' or 'brimstone', is the burning mineral of the judgment.
entities.summary_bio: What the LORD rains on Sodom and Gomorrah from the LORD out of heaven, overthrowing the cities, the plain, and all that grew.

components.evidence_explanation: Gen 19:38: Ben-ammi is 'the father of the children of Ammon to this day'.
Gen 19:36–38: both daughters conceive by their father and bear Moab and Ben-ammi.
Gen 19:23: the sun was risen upon the land when Lot entered Zoar; the town he chose as his refuge (19:20–22).

components.label_value: Living in a cave above Zoar

Gen 19:30: Lot left Zoar because he was afraid to live there.

systems.name: Angelic deliverance
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Divine messengers appear in many ancient narratives as agents who pull the faithful out of a coming disaster. In Genesis the deliverance is tied to the mercy of the LORD, and the rescued are told how to escape.
rules_and_mechanics: The messengers take the rescued by the hand and lead them out.
The rescue is credited to the mercy (chemlah) of the LORD.
The rescued must obey the terms: flee, and do not look back or stay in the plain.

systems.name: Divine judgment by fire from heaven
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Fire from the sky as divine punishment is a recurring picture of a god's wrath in ancient Near Eastern and biblical texts. The destruction of cities, plain and vegetation (compare Deut 29:23) is the reference case.
rules_and_mechanics: The LORD sends sulfur and fire from heaven.
The judgment falls on whole cities and their land, not only on individuals.
The righteous are delivered first, through a messenger, before it falls.

systems.name: Protection of a guest
systems.ancient_near_east_context: In the ancient Near East a host owed his guest protection once the guest had come under his roof, a duty that could outweigh the host's own household. Its violation was a grave offence, and in Gen 19 and Judg 19 the sin of the city is shown through it.
rules_and_mechanics: A guest under the host's roof is under the host's protection ('the shadow of my roof').
The host answers for the guest's safety, even at great cost to himself.
A traveller offered hospitality is not to be abused by the town.

systems.name: Preserving the line by intoxicating the father
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Continuing a family line mattered intensely in the patriarchal world, and the childless had few legitimate means. Here the means is deception and incest, which the text reports without comment, and which the later law forbids (Lev 18:7).
rules_and_mechanics: The daughters make their father drink wine so that he does not know.
One daughter lies with him each night, in turn.
The aim is children, to 'preserve seed' (mechayyeh zera') of the father.

systems.name: Supernatural blinding
systems.ancient_near_east_context: Sudden blindness (sanverim) is a rare act of divine defence, here and in 2 Kgs 6:18. It disables an enemy without killing and leaves those struck helpless.
rules_and_mechanics: It is worked by messengers of God, not by ordinary force.
It strikes a whole group at once, small and great.
Those blinded cannot find even the door.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The angels seize the hands of Lot, his wife and two daughters and lead them outside the city, telling them to flee and not look back.
system_instances.significance_note: Lot is saved by the mercy of the LORD, not by his own delay.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The visitors strike the men at the door with blindness, and they grope in vain for the door.
system_instances.significance_note: The visitors show themselves as divine messengers and protect Lot's household.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The LORD rains sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah, overthrowing the cities, the plain and all that lives there.
system_instances.significance_note: It is the judgment the LORD announced to Abraham in Gen 18.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The elder daughter and her sister make Lot drink wine, and she lies with him without his knowledge.
system_instances.significance_note: It is the first half of the origin of Moab.

system_instances.outcome_summary: God remembers Abraham and sends Lot out from the midst of the overthrow.
system_instances.significance_note: It ties Lot's escape to Abraham's intercession in Gen 18.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Lot goes out, shuts the door, begs the crowd not to act wickedly, and offers his two daughters instead of his guests.
system_instances.significance_note: It shows how absolutely the duty of a guest's protection weighs, and Lot's own moral cost.

system_instances.outcome_summary: After pressing them, Lot brings the visitors home and gives them a feast with unleavened bread.
system_instances.significance_note: It sets up the test of hospitality that Sodom fails.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Lot rises to meet the two visitors at the gate and bows with his face to the ground.
system_instances.significance_note: He treats strangers as honoured guests, in contrast with the city that follows.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.
system_instances.significance_note: It shows what happens to someone who disobeys the command not to look back, and what the rescue cost.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The next night the younger daughter lies with the drunk Lot.
system_instances.significance_note: It is the origin of Ben-ammi and the Ammonites.

edges.description: The visitors strike the men at the door with blindness, small and great.
Outside the city they tell Lot to flee for his life and not look back.
The speaker grants Lot's request and will not overthrow the small city.
The angels take hold of the hands of Lot, his wife and his daughters and lead them outside the city.
The visitors tell Lot to bring his family and all that is his out of the city.
The visitors reach out, pull Lot back into the house and shut the door.
The elder daughter bears a son and names him Moab.
The daughters make Lot drink wine on the first night.
The elder daughter lies with her father; he does not know when she lies down or rises.
The elder daughter tells her sister that they should make their father drink wine and lie with him to preserve his seed.
God sends Lot out of the midst of the overthrow.
God remembers Abraham as he overthrows the cities of the plain.
Lot rises to meet the two visitors and bows with his face to the ground.
Lot presses the visitors to enter his house and makes them a feast.
Lot offers the crowd his two virgin daughters in place of his guests.
Lot asks to escape to the small city nearby instead of the mountain.
Lot tells his sons-in-law to leave because the LORD will destroy the city; they take it for a joke.
The men of Sodom call for Lot to bring out his guests so that they may know them.
The crowd tells Lot they will treat him worse than his guests and presses to break the door.
The LORD rains sulfur and fire on Gomorrah.
The LORD rains sulfur and fire on Sodom.
The younger daughter bears a son and names him Ben-ammi.
The next night the younger daughter lies with her drunk father.
